title: Information Sensitivity Symbolic Standard
purpose: Add an information sensitivity and access-control layer to the symbolic standard so documents, passages, evidence, identity-linked information, private inner content, and harm-risk material can be classified before viewing is allowed.

core_definition.summary: This UKR classifies information by sensitivity level, special risk tags, viewer authorization, need-to-know, purpose limits, and harm risk. It prevents curiosity, proximity, technical access, claimed authority, or social connection from becoming permission to view restricted material.
core_definition.governing_rule: Information access must be classified before viewing is allowed. Access requires sensitivity classification, viewer authorization, need-to-know, owner permission where applicable, purpose limit, and scope control. Harm-risk information is restricted by default.
core_definition.core_rule_formula: Access = sensitivity_level + viewer_authorization + need_to_know + owner_permission + purpose_limit + scope_limit - harm_risk - overreach

core_separation.corrected_equation: view_permission = classification_level + authorization + need_to_know + purpose_limit + scope_limit
core_separation.one_line_translation: Not everyone gets to see everything. Access requires permission, purpose, and proof of need.

◈I.label: Internal
◈I.meaning: Normal private or internal information not meant for public view.
◈I.default_access: approved internal members or approved users

◆R.label: Restricted
◆R.meaning: Sensitive information requiring a specific reason to access.

⛔C.label: Confidential
⛔C.meaning: High-sensitivity information that could cause privacy harm, legal risk, reputational damage, exploitation, or personal vulnerability if exposed.
⛔C.default_access: named or explicitly approved viewers only

✦S.label: Secret
✦S.meaning: Critical private information where exposure creates serious harm, danger, compromise, or irreversible loss.

⌬ID.label: Identity-Sensitive
⌬ID.meaning: Information that identifies a real person, account, source, location, role, signature, or private association.
⌬ID.boundary: Identity information does not become public just because someone knows it.

▣EV.label: Evidence-Sensitive
▣EV.meaning: Records, logs, screenshots, documents, proof trails, claims, or investigative material.
▣EV.boundary: Evidence should not be casually shared, altered, or socially circulated.

☁PR.label: Private Inner Content
☁PR.meaning: Personal thoughts, drafts, symbolic/private material, imagination, journals, unpublished reflections.
☁PR.boundary: Private inner content does not become public conduct or misconduct just because someone reads it.

⛝HX.label: Harm / Exploit Risk
⛝HX.meaning: Information that could enable harassment, coercion, doxxing, theft, retaliation, hacking, manipulation, or abuse.
⛝HX.boundary: If access could enable harm, default to denial unless a legitimate safety, legal, or protective need is proven.

owner.meaning: The person or entity that owns or controls the material.
owner.default_access: full access to their own material unless legal or safety constraints apply

named_viewer.meaning: A person specifically approved to view an item.
named_viewer.default_access: can view only specifically shared items

trusted_handler.meaning: A person trusted to handle restricted or confidential material within a defined scope.

evidence_handler.meaning: A person authorized to handle evidence-sensitive material.
evidence_handler.default_access: access to ▣EV only within evidence integrity rules

admin.meaning: A person who can manage systems or permissions.
admin.default_access: can manage systems, but does not automatically view private content

public_viewer.meaning: Any ordinary viewer without special authorization.

classification_format.standard_tag: [Classification | Special Tags | Allowed Viewers | Restriction Reason | Scope]
classification_format.example: [⛔C | ⌬ID ▣EV | Owner + Evidence Handler | identity-linked private evidence | no public sharing]

field_rules.Allowed_Viewers: Name roles or specific authorized viewer classes.
field_rules.Scope: State the limit so access does not expand beyond the reason.

valid_access_rules.internal_rule: ◈I material requires approved membership or approved internal access.
valid_access_rules.confidential_rule: ⛔C material requires named access, purpose limit, and audit or tracking.
valid_access_rules.secret_rule: ✦S material requires minimum access, explicit authorization, and logging.
valid_access_rules.identity_rule: ⌬ID identifies; it does not grant ownership, guilt, authority, or public permission.
valid_access_rules.evidence_rule: ▣EV requires evidence integrity: preserve, restrict editing, track access.
valid_access_rules.private_inner_content_rule: ☁PR remains private inner content unless explicitly shared by the owner.
valid_access_rules.harm_risk_rule: ⛝HX is restricted by default; access must be justified by safety, legal, or protective need.
valid_access_rules.admin_boundary_rule: Admin capability is not automatic content-viewing permission.

symbolic_integration.integrated_processing_flow: ☁/▣ first → 17D context second → evidence third → mark fourth → sensitivity fifth → access decision last
symbolic_integration.access_decision_formula: view_permission := classification_level ∧ authorization ∧ need_to_know ∧ purpose_limit ∧ scope_limit ∧ ¬unjustified_harm_risk

distortion_tests.name: Curiosity Is Not Access Test
distortion_tests.question: Is someone treating curiosity, interest, or social pressure as permission to view?

distortion_tests.name: Technical Access Boundary Test
distortion_tests.question: Can the person open the item technically, but lack authorization to view it?

distortion_tests.name: Need-to-Know Test
distortion_tests.question: Does the viewer have a real need-to-know within scope?

distortion_tests.name: Identity Exposure Test
distortion_tests.question: Does the item identify a person, location, source, account, or private association?

distortion_tests.name: Evidence Integrity Test
distortion_tests.question: Could sharing or editing damage the integrity of evidence?

distortion_tests.name: Private Inner Content Test
distortion_tests.question: Is private symbolic or inner material being treated as if it is public conduct?

distortion_tests.name: Harm Enablement Test
distortion_tests.question: Could access enable harassment, coercion, doxxing, theft, retaliation, hacking, manipulation, or abuse?

distortion_tests.name: Authority Proof Test
distortion_tests.question: Has the viewer's claimed authority been verified?

failure_modes.name: Curiosity-as-Permission
failure_modes.description: A person wants to see information and treats that desire as access authorization.

failure_modes.name: Technical-Access Overreach
failure_modes.description: A person can open or retrieve content and falsely treats capability as permission.

failure_modes.name: Identity Exposure Drift
failure_modes.description: Identity-linked information is shared beyond its proper scope.

failure_modes.name: Evidence Circulation
failure_modes.description: Evidence-sensitive material is casually shared, edited, or socially circulated.

failure_modes.name: Private-Content Violation
failure_modes.description: Private inner content is viewed, exposed, or judged without consent.

failure_modes.name: Harm-Risk Leakage
failure_modes.description: Information that enables harm is disclosed to an unsafe or unjustified viewer.

failure_modes.name: Authority Impersonation
failure_modes.description: A viewer claims authority without proof and attempts to gain access.

psc_locks: Private content stays private unless shared.
Identity data has a scope lock.
Harm-risk data is restricted by default.
Not everyone gets to see everything.
Access requires permission, purpose, and proof of need.
